learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the deep, fragile connection between nature and human society, and how human actions cause ecological crises that threaten our very existence.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The idea that nature and society are deeply interconnected. How we interact with nature depends on how our society is organized. Environmental problems are actually social problems.
Using up non-renewable resources (like groundwater, coal, and petroleum) faster than they can be replaced. This causes major crises, especially for poor communities who depend directly on nature.
Air, water, and soil pollution are caused by unchecked industrialization. The emission of greenhouse gases leads to global warming, which changes weather patterns and melts ice caps.
Environmental disasters do not affect everyone equally. The rich can buy bottled water and ACs to escape pollution and heat, while the poor bear the brunt of ecological destruction.
Social movements organized to protect nature. A famous example is the Chipko Movement in the Himalayas, where women hugged trees to prevent them from being cut down by contractors.

fun_activity.title: 💧 The Water Audit
fun_activity.instructions: For one day, count how many times you turn on a tap. Imagine if you had to walk 2 kilometers to fetch all that water in buckets. Write down one way you can save water tomorrow!

exam_tips: 📌 Always connect environmental issues to social inequality. The poor rely on 'common property resources' (like rivers and forests), so when these are destroyed, their livelihood is destroyed.
📌 Be ready to write a short note on the 'Chipko Movement'—highlighting the role of women in environmental protection.
📌 Differentiate between natural ecology (the physical environment) and social ecology (how social structures shape the environment).
quick_recap: ⭐ The capitalist pursuit of endless profit is a major cause of environmental degradation.
⭐ Deforestation not only destroys habitats but also disrupts the water cycle, causing both floods and droughts.
⭐ Environmental management requires a shift from short-term greed to long-term sustainable development.
